headline_marked: 5 bullets found in body of [[journalist shot dead in Netrokona]]
headline: 5 bullets found in body of journalist shot dead in Netrokona
summary: Lutfuzzaman Alif, a representative of Ruposhi Bangla, was killed by gunmen on motorcycles in broad daylight at Utrail Bazar.
details: Lutfuzzaman Alif, a journalist for Ruposhi Bangla and administrator of the Facebook page 'Detective Article', was shot dead on Thursday night at Utrail Bazar in Durgapur, Netrokona.
Witnesses report that two youths on a motorcycle approached Alif while he was sitting at a shop around 8:15 PM and fired multiple shots at him before fleeing the scene.
Local residents rushed him to the Upazila Health Complex, but he died shortly after. Police officials confirmed that five bullets were found in his head, neck, and chest.
Netrokona Police Superintendent Mo. Tariqul Islam visited the scene, and police operations are currently underway to arrest the perpetrators.
This is not the first time Alif had been targeted; on November 10, he was hacked with sharp weapons in the Tairibazar Ghat area of the Someshwari River.
Reports indicate that the victim often wrote about drug smuggling on social media, which may be linked to the motive behind the attacks.
caption:
A journalist was shot 5 times in Netrokona. He had previously been attacked and hacked for reporting on drug smuggling.

Lutfuzzaman Alif, a journalist for Ruposhi Bangla and administrator of the Facebook page 'Detective Article', was shot dead on Thursday night at Utrail Bazar in Durgapur, Netrokona.

Witnesses report that two youths on a motorcycle approached Alif while he was sitting at a shop around 8:15 PM and fired multiple shots at him before fleeing the scene.

Local residents rushed him to the Upazila Health Complex, but he died shortly after. Police officials confirmed that five bullets were found in his head, neck, and chest.

Netrokona Police Superintendent Mo. Tariqul Islam visited the scene, and police operations are currently underway to arrest the perpetrators.

This is not the first time Alif had been targeted; on November 10, he was hacked with sharp weapons in the Tairibazar Ghat area of the Someshwari River.

Reports indicate that the victim often wrote about drug smuggling on social media, which may be linked to the motive behind the attacks.

headline_marked: 10 die in 24 hours as [[dengue surge overwhelms hospitals]]
headline: 10 die in 24 hours as dengue surge overwhelms hospitals
summary: The daily death toll hit a yearly high again, with 1,943 patients hospitalised in a single day according to the DGHS.
details: At least 10 dengue patients died and 1,943 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am yesterday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This marks the highest daily death toll recorded so far this year.
Of the deaths, four occurred in Dhaka South City Corporation, three in Dhaka North City Corporation, two in Chattogram division, and one in Dhaka division.
The total death toll for the year has now risen to 331, with total cases reaching 1,07,259.
Currently, 5,897 dengue patients are receiving treatment in hospitals across the country.
A similar peak of 10 deaths in a single day was previously recorded on October 6.
caption:
10 deaths in 24 hours. 1,943 hospitalisations. The dengue surge is hitting a yearly high.

At least 10 dengue patients died and 1,943 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am yesterday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

This marks the highest daily death toll recorded so far this year.

Of the deaths, four occurred in Dhaka South City Corporation, three in Dhaka North City Corporation, two in Chattogram division, and one in Dhaka division.

The total death toll for the year has now risen to 331, with total cases reaching 1,07,259.

Currently, 5,897 dengue patients are receiving treatment in hospitals across the country.

A similar peak of 10 deaths in a single day was previously recorded on October 6.

#Bangladesh #Dengue #HealthCrisis #DGHS #PublicHealth

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV
